chunks.text:
Atorvastatin is a prescription medicine.
Atorvastatin is used to treat high cholesterol.
Atorvastatin is used to reduce the risk of heart attack.
Atorvastatin is used to reduce the risk of stroke.
Atorvastatin is used to reduce the risk of angina.
Atorvastatin is used to decrease the chance that heart surgery will be needed.
Atorvastatin is used in people who have heart disease.
Atorvastatin is used in people who are at risk of developing heart disease.
Atorvastatin helps lower LDL cholesterol ('bad cholesterol') and triglyceride levels.
It increases HDL cholesterol ('good cholesterol') levels.
These actions improve your overall lipid profile.
Atorvastatin calcium belongs to a class of medications called HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, commonly referred to as statins.
Atrovastatin tablets are taken once daily with or without food.

chunks.text:
Atorvastatin works by selectively blocking HMG-CoA reductase.
HMG-CoA reductase is the key enzyme the liver uses to produce cholesterol.
Atorvastatin reduces cholesterol production in the liver.
Atorvastatin increases the number of LDL receptors on liver cells.
This helps remove more LDL ("bad") cholesterol from the bloodstream.
Atorvastatin works by slowing this process.
As a result, Atorvastatin lowers overall LDL levels.
It decreases the number of LDL particles.
It improves the body's ability to clear cholesterol.

chunks.text:
Atorvastatin FDA-approved uses:
To reduce the risk of cardiovascular events in adults with:
Multiple risk factors for coronary heart disease (CHD), but without established CHD.
Use: to reduce the risk of myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, revascularization procedures, and angina.
Type 2 diabetes and multiple risk factors for CHD, without established CHD Use: to help reduce the risk of MI and stroke.
Adults with clinically evident CHD should use this to reduce the risk of non-fatal MI.
It is used to reduce the risk of fatal and non-fatal stroke.
It is used to reduce the risk of revascularization procedures.
It is used to reduce the risk of hospitalization for congestive heart failure.
It is used to reduce the risk of angina.
As an adjunct to diet to lower LDL-C:
Adults with primary hyperlipidemia.
Adults and pediatric patients (10 years and older) with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH).
As an adjunct to other LDL-lowering therapies:
For adults and pediatric patients (10 years and older) with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia.

chunks.section_heading: How atorvastatin improves cholesterol and heart health
chunks.text:
When cholesterol and fats build up along your artery walls.
This process is called atherosclerosis.
Cholesterol and fats narrow the blood vessels.
This reduces blood and oxygen flow to your heart, brain, and other parts of your body.
Atorvastatin helps prevent this buildup.
This is done by slowing cholesterol production.
This keeps blood flowing more freely to vital organs.
Lowering your blood level of cholesterol and fats with atorvastatin may help prevent heart disease.
It may also help prevent angina (chest pain).
It may also help prevent strokes.
It may also help prevent heart attacks.
Your healthcare provider will check your blood lipid levels regularly to assess how well your treatment is working.
These measurements include:
LDL-C: Low-density lipoprotein (“bad” cholesterol)
HDL-C: High-density lipoprotein (“good” cholesterol)
TG: Triglycerides (a type of blood fat)
Total-C: Total cholesterol

chunks.text:
You should not take atrovastatin calcium if you have liver disease or cirrhosis.
Atorvastatin calcium can cause the breakdown of muscle tissue.
The breakdown of muscle tissue can lead to kidney failure.
Call your doctor right away if you have unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness.
Do so especially if you also have fever, unusual tiredness, or dark urine.
Serious drug interactions can occur when certain medicines are used together with atrovastatin calcium.
Tell each of your healthcare providers about all medicines you use now, and any medicine you start or stop using.
Avoid drinking more than 1.2 liters of grapefruit juice each day.
Avoid eating foods that are high in fat or cholesterol.
Atrovastatin is often used in conjunction with a cholesterol-lowering diet.

Common atorvastatin side effects:
Common atorvastatin side effects may include pain in your bones, spine, joints, or muscles.
Common atorvastatin side effects may include muscle spasms.
Common atorvastatin side effects may include upset stomach.
Common atorvastatin side effects may include trouble sleeping.
Common atorvastatin side effects may include a stuffy nose.
Common atorvastatin side effects may include a runny nose.
Common atorvastatin side effects may include a sore throat.
Common atorvastatin side effects may include diarrhea.
Common atorvastatin side effects may include nausea.
Common atorvastatin side effects may include pain in your arms or legs.
Common atorvastatin side effects may include a urinary tract infection with pain and burning when you urinate.
Common atorvastatin side effects may include painful urination.
Some people taking statins have reported memory loss, forgetfulness, or confusion.
These symptoms are usually not serious and go away after stopping Atorvastatin.

chunks.text:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to atorvastatin.
Signs of an allergic reaction include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Myopathy and Rhabdomyolysis are conditions related to Atorvastatin calcium.
Atorvastatin calcium can cause the breakdown of muscle tissue.
The breakdown of muscle tissue can lead to kidney failure.
Call your doctor right away if you have unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness.
Do so especially if you also have fever, unusual tiredness, or dark urine.
This serious side effect is more likely in older adults.
This serious side effect is more likely in those who have kidney problems.
This serious side effect is more likely in those who have thyroid problems.
This serious side effect is more likely in those who take certain other medicines.
Other serious side effects may occur.

You should not take atorvastatin if you have liver disease or cirrhosis.
Atorvastatin can cause the breakdown of muscle tissue.
The breakdown of muscle tissue can lead to kidney failure.
Call your doctor right away if you have unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness.
Do so especially if you also have fever, unusual tiredness, or dark urine.
Serious drug interactions can occur when certain medicines are used together with atorvastatin.
Tell each of your healthcare providers about all medicines you use now, and any medicine you start or stop using.
Avoid eating foods that are high in fat or cholesterol.
Atorvastatin will not be as effective in lowering your cholesterol.
This is because you do not follow a cholesterol-lowering diet plan.
Atorvastatin is only part of a complete program of treatment that also includes diet, exercise, and weight control.
Follow your diet, medication, and exercise routines very closely.

You should not use atorvastatin if you are allergic to atorvastatin.
You should not use atorvastatin if you have liver failure.
You should not use atorvastatin if you have cirrhosis.
To make sure atorvastatin is safe for you, tell your doctor if you have ever had:
muscle pain or weakness;
diabetes;
stroke;
a thyroid disorder;
a habit of drinking more than 2 alcoholic beverages per day; or
kidney disease.
Atorvastatin can cause the breakdown of muscle tissue.
The breakdown of muscle tissue can lead to kidney failure.
This happens more often in women.
This happens more often in older adults.
This happens more often in people who have kidney disease.
This happens more often in people who have poorly controlled hypothyroidism.
Pregnancy:
Tell your healthcare professional if you are pregnant, or plan to become pregnant, or become pregnant.
Atorvastatin may harm your unborn baby.
If you become pregnant, stop taking atorvastatin and call your healthcare provider right away.
Breastfeeding:
Tell your healthcare professional if you are breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed.

chunks.section_heading: What should I avoid while taking atorvastatin?
chunks.text:
Avoid eating foods high in fat or cholesterol.
Atorvastatin will not be as effective.
Drinking alcohol may increase your risk of liver damage.
Grapefruit may interact with atorvastatin and cause side effects.
Avoid consuming grapefruit products and drinking more than 1.2 liters of grapefruit juice each day.

chunks.section_heading: What other drugs will affect atorvastatin?
chunks.text:
Sometimes it is not safe to use certain medicines at the same time.
Some drugs can affect your blood levels of other drugs you use.
This can increase the risk of serious muscle problems.
This can make the medicines less effective.
Tell your doctor about all your current medicines.
Many drugs can interact with atorvastatin, especially:
other cholesterol-lowering medicines - gemfibrozil, niacin, fenofibrate, fenofibric acid, and others;
colchicine;
antibiotic or antifungal medicine - rifampin, erythromycin, clarithromycin, itraconazole, ketoconazole, posaconazole, and voriconazole;
birth control pills;
medicine to prevent organ transplant rejection; or
antiviral medicine to treat hepatitis C, HIV, or cytomegalovirus (such as letermovir).
This list is not complete.
Many other drugs may interact with atorvastatin.
List includes prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.
Not all possible drug interactions are listed here.
